title: 4.3 Related Rates

icans: I can write an equation that relates the changing quantities.
I can differentiate an equation with respect to time t.
I can solve related rate problems with circles, spheres, ladders, and cones.

vocab: rates of change of _____________ that are related by an equation
dx/dt, how fast x __________ per unit of time

blocks.p: A 10-cm ruler: x is the distance of the bottom from the book, y is the height of the top.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Step 1: draw a picture, name the variables, and write the given rates and the _______________ rate.
Step 2: write an equation that relates the _______________.

blocks.stem: The radius of a circle increases at 2 cm/s. How fast is the area increasing when r = 10 cm?

notes: Step 3: differentiate both sides with respect to _______________.

blocks.stem: Air is pumped into a spherical balloon at 100 cm³/s. How fast is the radius increasing when r = 5 cm?

notes: Step 4: substitute the values at the instant only _______________ differentiating.

blocks.stem: A 10-ft ladder leans against a wall. The bottom slides away at 1 ft/s. How fast is the top changing when the bottom is 6 ft from the wall?
Water pours into an inverted cone (radius 2 m, height 4 m) at 3 m³/min. How fast is the water rising when it is 2 m deep?
x² + y² = 25 with dx/dt = 2. Find dy/dt at (3, 4).
The side of a square increases at 3 cm/s. How fast is the area increasing when the side is 5 cm?

(AP® Practice) A spherical balloon is inflated at 32π cm³/s. How fast is the radius increasing when r = 2 cm?
(A) 2 cm/s   (B) 1/2 cm/s   (C) 8 cm/s   (D) 4 cm/s

tickets.stem: y = x² and dx/dt = 3. Find dy/dt when x = 4.
A circle’s radius grows at 1 cm/s. Find dA/dt when r = 3 cm.
Why do you substitute values only after differentiating?
